{"slug": "build-a-website-by-chatting-with-ai", "title": "Build a Website by Chatting With AI", "metaTitle": "Build a Website by Chatting With AI — Kodely", "metaDescription": "See exactly what it looks like to build a real website by chatting with Kodely — a turn-by-turn example, why chat beats a form, and what you actually get.", "targetKeyword": "build a website by chatting with ai", "category": "Feature", "bodyHtml": "

Most website builders still start with a form: pick a template, choose a color, fill in eight fields, click next. Kodely starts with a text box. You type what you want in plain English, and a real app gets built in front of you — not a mockup, an actual Vite + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS v4 codebase, compiling live as you watch.

Here is what that actually looks like, turn by turn.

A real conversation, start to finish

You: I need a landing page for a small-batch coffee roastery. Dark, moody, with a hero section, a section for our three current roasts, and an email signup at the bottom.

Kodely: Building it now — dark theme with a warm accent, hero with a full-bleed background, a three-card roast grid, and an email capture form at the bottom.

A few seconds later, the live preview renders: an actual compiled page, not a screenshot. You can scroll it, resize it, click into it.

You: The roast cards feel too plain. Add a price and a tasting-notes line to each one, and make the hero headline bigger.

Kodely: Updating the roast card component to include price and tasting notes, and increasing the hero headline size.

Kodely does not regenerate the whole site. It edits the specific components — the card layout, the hero typography — and the preview updates in place. Everything else on the page stays exactly as it was.

You: Perfect. Publish it.

Kodely: Site is live at yourroastery.kodely.site.

That is the entire loop: describe, watch it get built, correct anything that is off, publish. No dashboard full of settings, no separate hosting signup, no export step. And because every successful generation along the way is saved as a checkpoint, if a later change makes things worse, rolling back to any earlier version is free.

Why chat beats a form or a wizard

A form only has the fields someone thought to put on it. If you want a pricing table with a highlighted middle tier, or a testimonial carousel with exactly four quotes, or a footer that only shows on certain sections — a wizard makes you either dig for a setting that does not exist or accept a compromise.

Chat has no fixed field set. You describe the thing you actually want, in your own words, at whatever level of detail you feel like giving. Want to say make it feel more like a boutique agency site and less like a SaaS template? You can say that directly, and Kodely translates it into actual component and layout changes — not a slider, not a theme picker, a real edit to the code.

The same applies to fixes. You do not hunt through a settings panel to figure out which toggle controls card spacing. You just say the spacing feels cramped, and it gets fixed.

What is actually real here

A few things worth being specific about, because a lot of AI website tools blur these:

  • Real code, not a black box. Every project starts from a hand-built foundation codebase, and every change lands in actual .tsx component files. You can open the code view inside Kodely and read the exact source that is running.
  • Publish-time secret scanning. Before any site goes live at its *.kodely.site URL, Kodely scans it for accidentally-leaked API keys or secrets, so a careless prompt cannot ship a credential to the public internet.
  • One-click, actually live. Publish gives you a real public URL immediately — included, no separate hosting step, no extra cost.
  • Free rollback, always. Every successful build is a checkpoint. If a change breaks something you liked, go back to the version before it, at no cost.
  • You only pay for builds that work. Credits are metered from real AI cost, and a build that fails to compile is never charged — Kodely attempts one automatic repair first.

Worth being equally clear about what this is not, today: there is no backend, database, auth, or payment generation — this is frontend only. There are no custom domains yet, only *.kodely.site subdomains. There is no zip export; you can see and copy your code in-app, but downloading it as a file is not available yet. Editing happens through chat only — there is no click-to-edit visual mode.

Pricing, in plain terms

Every new account gets 750 credits free, no credit card required. When you need more, credits are simple top-ups that never expire:

Top-upCredits
$9500 credits
$40 (most popular)2,500 credits
$906,000 credits

See the full breakdown on the pricing page.

FAQ

Do I need to know how to code?

No. You describe what you want in plain English. Kodely writes and edits the actual React components for you.

Can I see the code it generates?

Yes — the code view inside Kodely shows the real source files as they are built, and you can copy them directly. There is no zip export yet.

What happens when I ask for a change?

Kodely edits the relevant components rather than rebuilding the whole site, so unrelated parts of your page stay untouched.

What if a generation breaks something?

Every successful build is a checkpoint. Roll back to any earlier version for free.

Do I get charged for failed builds?

No. A build that fails to compile is never charged, after one automatic repair attempt.

Can I use my own domain?

Not yet — published sites live at a free *.kodely.site subdomain.

How does this compare to other AI builders?

See our detailed comparison in Kodely vs. Lovable.

The fastest way to see this for yourself is to try it. Start building free — 750 credits, no credit card needed. Or check pricing first, browse the blog, or log in if you already have an account.
